title: Rate Lock Commitment Extension Cost: Length Booked, Larkspur-Borne Days and Charge
content:
**Rate Lock Commitment — extension cost.**

**1. Length booked.** The extension booked is the shortest of the lock's sold extension lengths that is at least the days asked for on the lock's latest extension request, never longer than the longest sold length. It is booked as the next extension in the lock's sequence, and its new expiration date is set under the extension policy.

**2. Per-day cost.** The per-day cost of an extension is the lock's extension cost per day in basis points, as set for the product.

**3. Larkspur-borne days.** The Larkspur-borne days of an extension are:

- the lock's complimentary extension days, when it is the lock's first extension (no extension entry is yet booked on the lock); plus
- the appraisal-delay days.

The appraisal-delay days are the calendar days by which the file's appraisal report was completed after its due date, never more than the lock's lender-delay allowance, less the lender-delay days already relieved on the lock. They are never below zero, and are counted in whole days with any fraction of a day dropped. The due date and the completed date are read from the **Appraisal Order**.

The lender-delay days already relieved are:

- the Larkspur-borne days booked on its earlier extensions beyond the complimentary days; plus
- for the lock's waiver entries, their waived dollars divided by the dollar value of one day at the lock's standard per-day cost. That dollar value is the loan amount at lock times the extension cost per day in basis points, divided by 10,000.

For an extension booked under this policy, Larkspur bears as many appraisal-delay days as the appraisal report was late, never more than the lender-delay allowance across the lock. Every lender-delay day already relieved on the lock, for any reason, counts against that allowance, not only the days borne for the appraisal delay. A waiver Larkspur books on its own initiative, and a decided extension-charge dispute, measure their days under their own rules.

*Hypothetical fraction:* if $100.00 has been waived on a lock where one day is worth $80.00, 1.25 days are already relieved. With an appraisal 4 days late, the appraisal-delay days are 4 less 1.25, which is 2.75, counted as 2 whole days.

**4. Charged days.** The charged days are the extension days less the Larkspur-borne days, never below zero.

**5. Cost.** The cost points are the charged days times the per-day cost divided by 100, rounded to three decimal places. The cost is the cost points times the loan amount at lock divided by 100, rounded to the cent.

### Worked example (hypothetical inputs, on a Larkspur 30-Day Rate Lock)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Days asked for on the latest extension request | 7 |
| Sold lengths of the product | 5, 10 and 15 days |
| Extension booked | 10 days (the shortest sold length of at least 7) |
| First extension on the lock | Yes; the product's complimentary days are 0 |
| Appraisal completed after its due date | 4 days; the allowance is 15 and nothing has been relieved yet, so 4 days |
| Larkspur-borne days | 0 plus 4, which is 4 |
| Charged days | 10 less 4, which is 6 |
| Per-day cost | 2.0 basis points |
| Cost points | 6 times 2.0 divided by 100, which is 0.120 |
| Loan amount at lock | $350,000.00 |
| Cost | 0.120 times $350,000.00 divided by 100, which is $420.00 |

*Hypothetical second case:* the same lock already carries one earlier extension with 3 Larkspur-borne days, all for an appraisal delay. The appraisal was 4 days late, so 3 lender-delay days are already relieved. A new 5-day extension carries 0 complimentary days, and 4 less 3, which is 1, appraisal-delay day. It is charged 4 days, at 2.0 basis points per day, for 0.080 points.

*Length boundary:* asked 0 days, the shortest sold length is booked. Asked 16 days on a product whose longest length is 15, 15 days are booked.
